newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to speed up satellite telecom opening.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to speed up satellite telecom opening.

text.p: Taiwan said on Wednesday it planned to speed up liberalisation of satellite communications, allowing private companies to operate mobile and fixed satellite telephone systems by the end of 1998.

"The latest plan is to open the market to private interests in the mobile and fixed satellite communications businesses by December 1998," an official at the Ministry of Transportation and Communications said.
The ministry originally wanted to open the satellite businesses by December 1999, the official added.
Taiwan's parliament passed three telecommunications laws in January 1996, opening up the island's long-closed telecom industry for private and limited foreign investment.
Under the laws, foreign investors can own stakes of up to 20 percent in Taiwan telecom ventures, though under some interpretations of the liberalised law foreigners can control up to 59 percent.
As part of its telecom liberalisation, Taiwan on Monday awarded eight mobile phone franchises to local consortiums, most of them paired with global telecom giants as minority partners.
